Inglewood, California
  April 16, 2024

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
April 16, 2024, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:01 p.m.

The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor Butts, Council Members Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Item No. CS-1.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session Item
No. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint Powers
Authority at the hour of 2:01 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Joint Powers
Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/ Joint Powers Authority Members,
  Padilla, Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing
  Authority Member/Joint Powers Authority Member Gray.

present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

Authority.

 April 16, 2024

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Faulk, and seconded by Council
  Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the demands
  presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated April 11, 2024,
  in the amount of $3,081,380.77, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members/
  Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Gray.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on February 6, 2024, February
  13, 2024, and February 27, 2024, be approved. The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

101  COOPERATIVE PURCHASE AGREEMENT NO. 24-180 APPROVED –
  UNIVERSAL PROTECTION SERVICE, LP DBA ALLIED UNIVERSAL
  SECURITY SERVICES (ALLIED UNIVERSAL); PAYMENT OF OUTSTANDING
  INVOICES AUTHORIZED – ALLIED UNIVERSAL. Staff report dated April 16,
  2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members approve a
  Cooperative Purchase Agreement with Universal Protection Service, LP, DBA Allied
  Universal Security Services (Allied Universal) for unarmed security officers at Inglewood
  City Hall, the Senior Center, Main Library, Crenshaw-Imperial Library, Morningside
  Library, and various City Parks.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Cooperative Purchase Agreement No. 24-180 in
  a total amount not to exceed $731,850.13; and 2) Authorize payment of outstanding invoices
  submitted by Allied Universal for unarmed security officer services provided for the months
  of September 2023 through March 2024, in a total amount not to exceed $534,803.25. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

301  ADVANCE FUNDS AGREEMENT NOT APPROVED – 308 E. BEACH LLC;
  ADVANCE FUNDS AGREEMENT NOT APPROVED – EAST BEACH
  INGLEWOOD, LLC; RESOLUTION NOT ADOPTED. This item was pulled from
  the Agenda.

178  PURCHASE ORDER FOR POLICE RADIOS APPROVED - MOTOROLA
  SOLUTIONS, INC. Staff report dated April 16, 2024, was presented recommending that
  the Mayor and Council Members authorize issuance of a purchase order to Motorola
  Solutions, Inc (Motorola) to purchase police radios.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby authorize issuance in a total amount not to exceed
  $489,239.96. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

  authorize payment of several invoices submitted by Aftermath Services, LLC for clean-up

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that

  was carried by the following roll call vote:

  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

132.9  CLOSED SESSION – PENDING LITIGATION – KAFSHI BENNETT V.
  INGLEWOOD POLICE DEPARTMENT. Closed Session – Confidential –
  Attorney/Client Privileged; City Council Conference with Legal Counsel regarding pending
  litigation pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1); Kafshi Bennett v.
  Inglewood Police Department; LASC Case No.: 24STCV01137.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve the request for settlement in the amount of $20,000.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

127.2  COUNCIL INITIATIVE

  Council Member Faulk:

  CITY SPONSORSHIP APPROVED AS MODIFIED – 2ND ANNUAL INGLEWOOD
  MUSICAL FESTIVAL. Initiative by Council Member Dionne Faulk recommending that
  the Mayor and Council Members approve City Sponsorship for the 2nd Annual Inglewood
  Music Festival to be held on Saturday, June 29, 2024, at Darby Park, in an amount not to
  exceed $150,000.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that the City
  Council does hereby approve the City Sponsorship of the 2nd Annual Inglewood Music
  Festival, in the amount not to exceed $100,000. The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke concerning the eight-year reopening of the Miracle
  Theater on Market Street by him and his wife. He mentioned that Netflix is a Joke will be
  at the Miracle Theatre in early May and the BET Experience in late June. He also mentioned
  that they work with many local community organizations and have an allotment of comp
  tickets. The Speaker stated that they are working with the Adult Services Group at the
  Inglewood Public Library for some of the shows and wanted to extend the opportunity for
  comp tickets for anyone who wanted to attend. Finally, he noted that the Miracle Theatre
  has some good shows coming up for those interested in attending.

  3
 April 16, 2024

  Wesley Crunk, a Local 323 Carpenters Union Member, spoke concerning local tax fraud.
  He stated that local tax fraud cheats communities out of billions of dollars in tax revenue.
  He also stated that the billions of dollars of lost tax revenue could be used to build and
  renovate schools, repair roads, care for veterans, shelter the unhoused, and fund other
  essential public programs. Mr. Crunk reported that the prevalence of construction industry
  tax fraud has reached crisis levels and must be stopped. He also discussed that Western State
  Carpenters Local 323 and The United Brotherhood of Carpenters were taking part in the
  National Tax Fraud Days of Action on April 13-19, 2024. Mr. Crunk explained that this
  event was a week-long series to raise awareness of widespread outrage about construction
  industry tax fraud. He further explained that construction tax fraud is a range of practices where
  employers evade their tax responsibilities by intentionally misclassifying workers as
  independent contractors or paying workers in cash-only arrangements. He added that
  businesses reduce their income tax and payroll tax responsibilities and defraud communities
  of much-needed tax revenues as they face budget shortfalls. Finally, he said that it was
  essential to crack down on employers as they were stealing from the residents of Inglewood.

  Tyriq Flint, Brother’s Keeper Pre-Apprenticeship Program Carpenters Union Member,
  spoke concerning tax fraud. He stated that tax fraud harms working families by employers
  shifting the tax burden onto employees. Mr. Flint also noted that employers  pay
  employment taxes out of their pockets, which burdens working families. He  addressed that
  if employees get sick or hurt on the job, they have no health benefits, nor are they eligible for
  worker’s comp. Mr. Flint mentioned that bad-actor employers are preying  on  vulnerable
  workers, taking advantage of the immigrant population, and  undercutting the competition.
  Finally, he reiterated that the bad actors are employers  defrauding working families and
  communities by doing business that fattens their wallets.

  Michael Carrion spoke about his telephone call to his Council Member's office. He stated
  he wanted to discuss a city vehicle parked three feet from the curb, which caused him to almost
  have an accident. Mr. Carrion shared about his conversation with the Inglewood Police
  Department, and he said the City would be held liable if someone had an accident.  He also
  discussed that they would be ticketed if someone else's car was parked three feet from the curb.
  Finally, he addressed his complaint regarding the Inglewood Police  Department.

  Tyson Baker, Inglewood Clothing Marketing Director and Brand Manager, spoke to inform
  the residents about the Inglewood Summer Concert Series. He stated it would be a concert
  and resource fair geared towards job placement and development, entrepreneurship, parent
  and child resources, and health and wellness (mental, physical, and emotional). Mr.
  Baker proposed holding the event at Centinela Park, now Edward Vincent Jr. Park. He
  reiterated awareness of this event planned for the summer and requested full support from
  the Council. Mr. Baker mentioned a pitch deck he submitted to the Parks and
  Recreation Department and wished God’s blessings on everyone.

  Marielle (Last Name Unknown) spoke concerning Inglewood's education system. She
  wanted to bring it to the council's attention because it is a growing problem. She also stated
  that since 2019, there have been three school closures, which have been a burden on parents and
  children. Finally, she noted that it had caused the education system to  decline.

  Daniella (Last Name Unknown) spoke concerning Inglewood’s education system. She
  expressed her fear that more schools would close, pushing families to send their children
  to schools outside of Inglewood or other cities. Daniella also expressed her concern that this
  would be an equity concern regarding financial burdens and transportation. Finally,  she
  suggested that some of the profits or revenue from SoFi Stadium be reinvested in schools.

  Council Member Morales left the dais at the hour of 2:21 p.m.

  Council Member Morales returned to the dais at the hour of 2:23 p.m.

  Sheree Danielle, 4K More Creative CEO & Executive Director, spoke concerning her
  vision to identify and develop 4,000 more creative leaders within the next ten years to
  provide them with equitable and sustainable jobs in the entertainment and production

  4
 April 16, 2024

  industry. She said Inglewood has incredible opportunities, and she discussed employing
  some of the creative leaders for the sound stages at Hollywood Park Casino with Mark
  Weinberg before the Christmas break. She also stated that she wanted to introduce herself
  and raise awareness about the many talented creative entrepreneurs in the city, especially
  regarding the upcoming Olympics. She discussed the panel the Mayor was scheduled to
  speak on and said she looked forward to hearing him speak. In her remarks, she emphasized
  the potential for creative leaders to become millionaires within the next few years. She also
  pointed out that financial opportunities could assist with funding the school and purchasing
  homes. Additionally, she announced the chance to learn more about Sheree 4K Moore's
  vision to help the creative economy, specifically for black and brown creatives. Finally, she
  mentioned loving the opportunity to speak with the Council to discuss getting more
  creatives into the vast entertainment conglomerates in the City of Inglewood.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in the memory of Steve Heineman, Santa Monica Police Department Lieutenant
  at the hour of 2:26 p.m.
